deep.reconstruction:
This page sits on the blank back of Cray-1 printout paper dated June 1982, so it predates Pursuing Stacks (Feb. 1983). It has two parts.

(1) Top, struck through with a large X. Let Y be a Kan complex (more generally a presheaf on a test category A with an interval I). The path-space map Hom(I,Y) -> Y x Y, evaluation at the two ends of I, is a Kan fibration when Y is Kan. This is the standard exponential (pushout-product) argument applied to the boundary inclusion {0,1} -> I. Grothendieck then asks whether it is also a fibration in some other (Serre-type?) sense. He starts to write the fibres sectionwise: for an object a of A, a map a -> Y x Y means a pair alpha, beta in Y_a. The fibre is Hom_{alpha,beta}(I_a, Y_a). He notes it is functorial in a -> b. The thread is abandoned.

(2) Main part: axioms for a class W of 'weak equivalences' in a category M.
- (a) Iso_M is contained in W.
- (b) Two out of three.
- (c) W is stable under retracts ('direct factors').
The right margin reads roughly '=> mild[?] 2-derivators'. Grothendieck asks whether (a)-(c) imply 'saturation': for f: A -> B and g: B -> A, fg in W and gf in W imply f, g in W.

He isolates three conditions:
- (i) gf = id_A and fg in W imply f, g in W. This is exactly Grothendieck's later 'weakly saturated' axiom.
- (ii) gf in W and fg in W imply f, g in W.
- (iii) W is stable under direct factors (retracts).
He records (ii) => (i) <= (iii).

Proof of (iii) => (i), drawn in the middle diagram: when gf = id_A, the arrow f: A -> B is a retract of fg: B -> B.
- Top row: A --f--> B --g--> A, composite id_A.
- Bottom row: B --id--> B --id--> B.
- Verticals: f, fg, f.
- The squares commute because fg∘f = f and f∘g = fg.
So f is in W by (c), and then g is in W by 2-out-of-3, since gf = id.
(ii) => (i) is trivial because id_A is in W.

The square with i, p, j, q writes out retract-stability explicitly:
- f'i = jf and fp = qf';
- pi = id_A and qj = id_B;
- f' in W implies (?) f in W.

The last sketch is the intended application. If gf is homotopic (relation h_W) to id_A and fg is homotopic to id_B, then gf and fg are in W ('done'). Hence (ii) would give that homotopy equivalences lie in W. The homotopy is written via cylinder data X <- I x X and path/diagonal data X -> X x X, with a marked point d of an interval.

The next page continues: in Quillen closed model categories W is stable under direct factors and even strongly saturated (f in W iff gamma(f) is an isomorphism).

The problem served: finding the minimal 'saturation' axioms on W for the theory of modelizers/derivators later developed in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs.
errors: The open question 'does a), b), c) imply saturation (ii)?' has a negative answer, which the page does not record. Take M = the free monoid on one generator x (one object), and W = the even powers of x. W contains the identity and satisfies 2-out-of-3. It is trivially retract-closed, since pi = 1 forces p = i = 1, and (i) also holds. But x·x is in W while x is not, so (ii) fails. Hence (ii) is genuinely stronger than (i)+(iii).
The top fibration discussion is fine as far as it goes ('Kan if Y Kan'). The question about a further fibration property is left unanswered.

ideas.what: Hom(I,Y) -> Y x Y is a Kan fibration for Y Kan (path-space fibration via exponentials).
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (discussion of intervals and fibrations)

ideas.what: Condition (i): gf = id and fg in W imply f, g in W.
ideas.modern_name: Weakly saturated class of weak equivalences (axiom FS3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, Pursuing Stacks; systematized by Maltsiniotis (Astérisque 301, 2005)

ideas.what: Condition (ii): gf and fg in W imply f, g in W.
ideas.modern_name: Special case of the 2-out-of-6 property (implied by saturation)

ideas.what: Retract-closure (iii) implies weak saturation (i), via f being a retract of fg when gf = id.
Homotopy equivalences lie in W once W satisfies (ii) and homotopic-to-identity maps are in W.

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly asks whether 2-out-of-3 plus retract-stability implies the two-sided saturation fg, gf in W => f, g in W. He records only (ii) => (i) <= (iii). The comparison he is groping for is essentially the later 2-out-of-6 versus weak-saturation hierarchy. The simple counterexample is not on the page.
missed.quote: but does it imply saturation, namely fg∈W, gf∈W ⇒ f,g∈W?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a dated (1982) early appearance of the axioms later called weakly saturated, and of a 2-out-of-6-type condition, two decades before DHKS. It is of historical interest only; the mathematics is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary axiom-juggling. Its only interest is dating: the 'weakly saturated' axiom and a 2-out-of-6-type condition appear in June 1982 material, before Pursuing Stacks.
transcription_corrections: Middle diagram: the vertical arrows are f, fg (marked ∈W) and f, with top rows A --=--> A and A --f--> B and bottom row B --id--> B. It exhibits f as a retract of fg. It is not simply a list of arrows.
'fg∈ id_A' should read 'gf = id_A' (with the condition fg ∈ W), consistent with (i) at the bottom.
Margin '⇒ mild[?] 2-derivators[?]' is highly uncertain. It could be 'milder localizations' or similar.
'(iii) W stable by direct factors' (= retracts). The struck words are likely 'by passing to', not 'functors'.
Retract square: the maps are p, i (between A and A') and q, j (between B and B'). The transcription's 'g,j' should be 'q,j'.
